subject: physics
title: Kinetic Theory and Internal Energy
welcome_lead: Connect microscopic motion to macroscopic temperature with ½ m c² = 3/2 kT.
meta_desc: A-Level Thermal Physics adventure on kinetic theory linking T to particle KE.
final_note: Temperature is just the mean kinetic energy of particles in disguise.

concepts.def: Model treating gas as fast-moving particles.
Average of v² across all particles.
½ m c² = 3/2 kT per molecule.
Sum of KE + PE of all particles.
U = 3/2 N k T (only translational KE).

walkthroughs.body_html: Pressure arises from molecular impacts. Result: pV = ⅓ N m c² where c² is mean square speed. Combine with pV = NkT to get ½ m c² = 3/2 kT.
Mean translational KE per molecule = 3/2 kT. Higher T = faster particles. At T = 0 K, motion stops (classically).
For ideal monatomic gas, all internal energy is translational KE: U = N × 3/2 kT = 3/2 nRT. Real molecules also have rotational and vibrational modes.

mcqs.q: Is the internal energy of a system the same as the heat it contains?
options: No — a system doesn't 'contain heat'; internal energy is the total kinetic and potential energy of its particles, changed by heating or doing work.
No — internal energy refers only to the chemical potential energy.
Yes — internal energy is just the stored heat in the object.
Kinetic energy stays the same because mass hasn't changed.

mcqs.q: If a car doubles its speed, what happens to its kinetic energy?
options: Kinetic energy stays the same because mass hasn't changed.
Kinetic energy doubles because energy is proportional to speed.
Energy has been converted into mass following E=mc^2.
It quadruples (because KE = 1/2 mv^2 — kinetic energy is proportional to v^2).

mcqs.q: When energy is 'lost' as heat due to friction, what has really happened?
options: Energy has been converted into mass following E=mc^2.
Kinetic energy stays the same because mass hasn't changed.
Energy has been transferred to the thermal store of the surroundings — it's not destroyed, just dissipated.
Energy has been used up and no longer exists.
